title: Trishanku seeks shelter with Vishvamitra
introduction: Trishanku seeks shelter of Vishvamitra when the sons of Vashishta rebuffed him, and even cursed him to become a profaner. Narrating his sad tale and his idealistic idea of going to heaven with mortal body, Trishanku earnestly appeals to Vishvamitra.
closing: इति वाल्मीकिरामायणे आदिकाव्ये बालकाण्डे अष्टपंचाशः सर्गः
Thus, this is the 58th chapter in Bala Kanda of Valmiki Ramayana, the First Epic poem of India.

verses.devanagari:
ततः त्रिशंकोर्वचनं श्रुत्वा क्रोधसमन्वितम् |
ऋषिपुत्रशतं राम राजानमिदमब्रवीत्
verses.iast:
tataḥ triśaṅkoḥ vacanam śrutvā krodha samanvitam |
ṛṣi putra śatam rāma rājānam idam abravīt
verses.translation: "On hearing the sentence of Trishanku, oh, Rama, the hundred sons of sage Vashishta infuriately said this to that king." Thus, sage Shataananda continued his narration to Rama and others.

verses.devanagari:
प्रत्याख्यातोऽसि दुर्बुद्धे गुरुणा सत्यवादिना |
तं कथं समतिक्रम्य शाखान्तरमुपेयिवान्
verses.iast:
pratyākhyāto asi durbuddhe guruṇā satya vādinā |
tam katham samatikraṃya śākhā antaram upeyivān
verses.translation: " 'You slow-witted king, your veracious mentor has denounced you. But transgressing him how do you approach another branch of the same tree of wisdom, when that very tree rejected you?' So the sons of Vashishta have started to denounce Trishanku.

glosses.itrans: satya vaadinaa guruNaa prati aakhyaataH asi
glosses.iast: satya vādinā guruṇā prati ākhyātaḥ asi
glosses.devanagari: सत्य वादिना गुरुणा प्रति आख्यातः असि
glosses.meaning: truth, advocator of, by mentor [Vashishta,] against, said [denounced,] you are

verses.devanagari:
इक्ष्वाकूणां हि सर्वेषां पुरोधाः परमा गतिः |
न चातिक्रमितुं शक्यं वचनं सत्यवादिनः
verses.iast:
ikṣvākūṇām hi sarveṣām purodhāḥ paramā gatiḥ |
na ca atikramitum śakyam vacanam satya vādinaḥ
verses.translation: " 'The Royal Priest is the ultimate course for all of Ikshvaku-s, isn't it. It is impossible to transgress the word of advise of such a veracious Priest.

glosses.meaning: Royal Priest is, ultimate, course, isn't it

verses.devanagari:
अशक्यमिति सोवाच वसिष्ठो भगवानृषिः |
तं वयं वै समाहर्तुं क्रतुं शक्ताः कथंचन
verses.iast:
aśakyam iti sa uvāca vasiṣṭho bhagavān ṛṣiḥ |
tam vayam vai samāhartum kratum śaktāḥ kathañcana
verses.translation: " 'Vashishta is the most reverential sage and such a sage has already said it is impossible to conduct such a Vedic-ritual. Then, in which way we are capable to conduct such a Vedic-ritual?

verses.devanagari:
बालिशस्त्वं नरश्रेष्ठ गम्यतां स्वपुरं पुनः |
याजने भगवान् शक्तस्त्रैलोक्यस्यापि पार्थिव
अवमानं कथं कर्तुं तस्य शक्ष्यामहे वयम् |
verses.iast:
bāliśaḥ tvam nara śreṣṭha gaṃyatām sva puram punaḥ |
yājane bhagavān śaktaḥ trailokyasya api pārthiva
avamānam katham kartum tasya śakśāyāmahe vayam |
verses.translation: " 'Oh king of subjects, better get back to your own city again for you are childish. That godlike Vashishta alone is capable to orchestrate any ritual by any king in all the three worlds. Oh, king, how then we are capable to cause a disrepute to his reputation.' Thus, the sons of Vashishta refuted Trishanku.

glosses.meaning: for men, the best [here, king of subjects]
again, [to your] own, city, get back
in orchestration of ritual, is capable

verses.devanagari:
तेषां तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा क्रोधपर्याकुलाक्षरम्
स राजा पुनरेवैतानिदं वचनमब्रवीत् |
verses.iast:
teṣām tad vacanam śrutvā krodha paryākula akṣaram
sa rājā punaḥ eva etān idam vacanam abravīt |
verses.translation: "On hearing that sentence of theirs which is highly faltering with words of fury that king further spoke this sentence to all of them." So Shataananda continued.

glosses.meaning: with fury, highly faltering, having words
from them, that, sentence, on hearing
to all of them, this, sentence, spoke.

verses.devanagari:
प्रत्याख्यातो भगवता गुरुपुत्रैस्तथैव हि
अन्यां गतिं गमिष्यामि स्वस्ति वोऽस्तु तपोधनाः |
verses.iast:
pratyākhyāto bhagavatā guru putraiḥ tathaiva hi
anyām gatim gamiṣyāmi svasti vo astu tapo dhanāḥ |
verses.translation: " 'I am indeed rejected by the godlike Vashishta, likewise even by you, the sons of the same mentor, as such oh, ascetically wealthy scholars, in this state obloquy I will resort to another recourse, let safety betide you.' So Trishanku bade farewell to the sons of Vashishta, but...

glosses.meaning: another, objective, I wish to reach at

verses.devanagari:
ऋषिपुत्रास्तु तच्छ्रुत्वा वाक्यं घोराभिसंहितम्
शेपुः परमसंक्रुद्धाश्चण्डालत्वं गमिष्यसि |
verses.iast:
ṛṣi putrāḥ tu tat śrutvā vākyam ghora abhisaṃhitam
śepuḥ parama saṅkruddhāḥ caṇḍālatvam gamiṣyasi |
verses.translation: "But the sons of the sage Vashishta, on hearing that sentence of the king, that is inclusive of and leading to a calamitous situation, have become very highly infuriated and cursed saying, 'you shall get into a state of basely profaner.' That is the curse issued by the sons of Vashishta to Trishanku.
notes: This expression caṇḍāl has its own impact. The nomenclature of caṇḍāl is not the present day 'untouchable' 'outcaste' or a 'pariah' etc., because he is also a member and an important functionary in Hindu system of castes. In Aranya Kanda Seetha admonishes Ravana with the same wording at 3-56-18. The analogy she uses there is to differentiate between functionaries like the Vedic-scholar and the caste-bound Profaner [meaning: one who is not initiated into religious rites or any esoteric knowledge... but socially designated as a Cremator] and between the Altar of Fire and Fire of Pyre, and between the Vedic Ritual and Funeral Rites, both involving Vedic-hymns. A Vedic scholar, or a true Brahmin may perhaps conduct a yajña but he is no authority to conduct antya kriya 'funerals' till its end. At best, a priest's function is until the lighting of the pyre, and even perhaps until kapāla mokśa 'breakage of cranium...' and from then on it is the function of this caṇḍāl to take care of the corpse consigned to fire and for its complete cremation, since leaving half burnt corpse to vultures and wolves is sinning as well as for unsanitary situations. Thus, if a Vedic scholar conducts jāta ādi kriyāḥ 'rites from birth onwards...' as an initiator, then a caṇḍāl conducts antya, uttara kriyāḥ 'rites of death afterwards...' as a terminator. This verbiage is to demark the relative values of functionaries, according to the maxim 'a donkey is to bear and a dog is to bark...' and if their functions are reversed, reversed are our results.

glosses.meaning: calamity, towards, well, inclusive of [an idea inclusive of and leading towards a calamitous situation]
state of a [basely] profaner, you get into

verses.devanagari:
इत्युक्त्वा ते महात्मानो विविशुः स्वं स्वमाश्रमम्
अथ रात्र्यां व्यतीतायां राजा चण्डालतां गतः |
verses.iast:
iti uktvā te mahātmāno viviśuḥ svam svam āśramam
atha rātryām vyatītāyām rājā caṇḍālatām gataḥ |
verses.translation: "On saying thus those great-souled sons of Vashishta withdrew to one's own hermitage and when that night elapsed into day then the king lapsed into a state of basely profaner.

glosses.meaning: [into their] own, [their] own, hermitage, entered - they withdrew
king, state of basely profaner, entered into.

verses.devanagari:
नीलवस्त्रधरो नीलः परुषो ध्वस्तमूर्धजः
चित्यमाल्यानुलेपश्च आयसाभरणोऽभवत् |
verses.iast:
nīla vastra dharo nīlaḥ paruṣo dhvasta mūrdhajaḥ
citya mālya anulepaḥ ca āyasa ābharaṇo abhavat |
verses.translation: "He is now wearing blackish cloths which on yestereve were ochry silks, he is now a blackamoor who on yestereve was a gilt-royalty, his head-hair is shaggy which earlier was silkily soft, and his royal garlands which were richly fragrant are now funeral wreaths, and he is besmeared with crematory ashes which were regal emollients, and his royal jewellery is now rendered into iron adornments.

glosses.meaning: one lacking gentleness or refinement - rugged person

verses.devanagari:
तं दृष्ट्वा मंत्रिणः सर्वे त्यक्त्वा चण्डालरूपिणम्
प्राद्रवन् सहिता राम पौरा येऽस्यानुगामिनः |
verses.iast:
tam dṛṣṭvā mantriṇaḥ sarve tyajya caṇḍāla rūpiṇam
prādravan sahitā rāma paurā ye asya anugāminaḥ |
verses.translation: "On seeing him in the mien of a profaner, oh, Rama, all of his ministers and the subjects and his own retinue have deserted him and took to flight in masses.

glosses.meaning: collectively - in masses, took to flight

verses.devanagari:
एको हि राजा काकुत्स्थ जगाम परमात्मवान्
दह्यमानो दिवारात्रं विश्वामित्रं तपोधनम् |
verses.iast:
eko hi rājā kākutstha jagāma parama ātmavān
dahyamāno divā rātram viśvāmitram tapo dhanam |
verses.translation: "Though that resolutely self-assured king seethed for one night and day for this mishap, then went to the ascetically prosperous Vishvamitra.

glosses.meaning: to ascetically, prosperous one, to Vishvamitra, went.

verses.devanagari:
विश्वामित्रस्तु तं दृष्ट्वा राजानं विफलीकृतम्
चण्डालरूपिणं राम मुनिः कारुण्यमागतः |
verses.iast:
viśvāmitraḥ tu tam dṛṣṭvā rājānam viphalī kṛtam
caṇḍāla rūpiṇam rāma muniḥ kāruṇyam āgataḥ |
verses.translation: But on seeing at that mien of the king which is rendered to that of a precluded profaner from kingship and for officiating rituals etc., oh, Rama, sage Vishvamitra because sympathetic. [1-58-13b, 14a].
notes: The preclusion of the king by way of his transfiguring into a profaner is not only from his kingship, by which he is debarred from officiating Vedic rituals etc., but also from his aihika āmuṣmika bhogāḥ 'earthly and heavenly enjoyments...' because a king is a godsend being.

glosses.meaning: without, fruit [failed, precluded one,] made as

verses.devanagari:
कारुण्यात्स महातेजा वाक्यं परमधार्मिकः
इदं जगाद भद्रं ते राजानं घोरदर्शनम् |
verses.iast:
kāruṇyāt sa mahātejā vākyam parama dhārmikaḥ
idam jagāda bhadram te rājānam ghora darśanam |
verses.translation: "The great-resplendent sage and highly generous Vishvamitra firstly said to that king who is in a terrible aspect 'let safety betide you,' and then spoke on this sentence to him.

glosses.meaning: who is terrible, in his aspect, to king

verses.devanagari:
किमागमनकार्यं ते राजपुत्र महाबल
अयोध्याधिपते वीर शापाच्चण्डालतां गतः |
verses.iast:
kim āgamana kāryam te rājaputra mahābala
ayodhyā adhipate vīra śāpāt caṇḍālatām gataḥ |
verses.translation: " 'What is the purpose of your visit, oh, great-mighty prince Trishanku, oh, brave lord of Ayodhya, you are accurst to the state of profaner.'

glosses.meaning: by curse, state of profaner, you got [accurst.]

verses.devanagari:
अथ तद्वाक्यमाकर्ण्य राजा चण्डालतां गतः
अब्रवीत् प्रांजलिर्वाक्यं वाक्यज्ञो वाक्यकोविदम् |
verses.iast:
atha tat vākyam ākarṇya rājā caṇḍālatām gataḥ
abravīt prāñjaliḥ vākyam vākyajño vākya kovidam |
verses.translation: "Then that king who is accurst to a state of profaner on listening that sentence, as a diligent sentence maker spoke this sentence with his palms adjoined to the sententious sage Vishvamitra.

glosses.meaning: sentence, knower, king - diligent king, Trishanku
with adjoined-palms, to sentence, expert [sententious Vishvamitra,] sentence, spoke.

verses.devanagari:
प्रत्याख्यातोऽस्मि गुरुणा गुरुपुत्रैस्तथैव च
अनवाप्यैव तं कामं मया प्राप्तो विपर्ययः |
verses.iast:
pratyākhyāto asmi guruṇā guru putraiḥ tathā eva ca
anavāpya eva tam kāmam mayā prāpto viparyayaḥ |
verses.translation: " 'I am spurned off by my mentor Vashishta and also like that by his sons. My aspiration remained unachievable, besides, this discrepancy has bechanced upon me.

verses.devanagari:
सशरीरो दिवं यायामिति मे सौम्य दर्शन
मया चेष्टं क्रतुशतं तच्च नावाप्यते फलम् |
verses.iast:
sa śarīro divam yāyāmi iti me sauṃya darśana
mayā ca iṣṭam kratu śatam tat ca na avāpyate phalam |
verses.translation: " 'Oh, gentle Vishvamitra, my aspiration is nothing but to go to heaven with my body. I have performed hundred rituals but I have not achieved the fruit.' Thus Trishanku started tell his sad tale.

glosses.meaning: with, body, to heaven, I go
by me, rituals, hundred, are performed [earlier]

verses.devanagari:
अनृतं नोक्तपूर्वं मे न च वक्ष्ये कदाचन
कृच्छ्रेष्वपि गतः सौम्य क्षत्रधर्मेण ते शपे |
verses.iast:
anṛtam na ukta pūrvam me na ca vakṣye kadācana
kṛcchreṣu api gataḥ sauṃya kṣatra dharmeṇa te śape |
verses.translation: " 'And now if you doubt me to be a liar, I am no liar either. I spoke no lie heretofore, and even if I were to land into any predicament I do not speak lies anytime hereinafter. Oh, gentle sage, this I pledge you upon my virtue of Kshatriya-hood.
notes: A liar is hell-bound but not the other way as said yajño anṛte na rakśati... 'a Vedic ritual would not save liars...'

glosses.meaning: into predicament, on going, even if
by Kshatriya's, virtue, to you, I take pledge.

verses.devanagari:
यज्ञैर्बहुविधैरिष्टं प्रजाधर्मेण पालिताः
गुरवश्च महात्मानः शीलवृत्तेन तोषिताः |
verses.iast:
yajñaiḥ bahu vidhaiḥ iṣṭam prajā dharmeṇa pālitāḥ
guravaḥ ca mahātmānaḥ śīla vṛttena toṣitāḥ |
verses.translation: " 'I have propitiated gods with many kinds of Vedic-rituals. I have reigned over people conscientiously. And with my conduct and comport the high-souled savants are also pleased.

glosses.meaning: with many, kinds of, Vedic-rituals, propitiated gods

verses.devanagari:
धर्मे प्रयतमानस्य यज्ञं चाहर्तुमिच्छतः
परितोषं न गच्छन्ति गुरवो मुनिपुंगव |
verses.iast:
dharme prayatamānasya yajñam ca āhartum icchataḥ
paritoṣam na gacchanti guravo munipuṅgava |
verses.translation: " 'While I am a pursuant in probity I expect to avail myself of the fruition of this kind of Vedic-ritual. Oh, eminent sage Vishvamitra, but my mentors are not deriving complete contentment by my pursuit. Hence, they shove me off.

glosses.meaning: ritual, to avail of, icChataH ca = one who is expectant also
complete contentment, na gacChanti = not, they are getting at - not deriving.

verses.devanagari:
दैवमेव परं मन्ये पौरुषं तु निरर्थकम्
दैवेनाक्रम्यते सर्वं दैवं हि परमा गतिः |
verses.iast:
daivam eva param manye pauruṣam tu nirarthakam
daivena ākraṃyate sarvam daivam hi paramā gatiḥ |
verses.translation: " 'I deem destiny is the only ultimate, and manly efforts are meaningless, for destiny surmounts everything. Destiny is the ultimate course, isn't it?

glosses.meaning: god [here, destiny,] only, ultimate, I deem
manly effort, but, less, meaning - meaningless

verses.devanagari:
तस्य मे परमार्तस्य प्रसादमभिकांक्षतः |
कर्तुमर्हसि भद्रं ते दैवोपहतकर्मणः
verses.iast:
tasya me parama ārtasya prasādam abhikāṅkṣataḥ |
kartum arhasi bhadram te daiva upahata karmaṇaḥ
verses.translation: " 'A highly anguished endeavourer, marred by destiny, a sincere requester, such as I am, it will be apt of you to accord, you be safe, your favour upon me. [1-58-23b, c]

glosses.meaning: forward, looking to - a sincere requester
favour, to do [to accord,] apt of you
to you, let safety be there.

verses.devanagari:
नान्यां गतिं गमिष्यामि नान्यः शरणमस्ति मे |
दैवं पुरुषकारेण निवर्तयितुमर्हसि
verses.iast:
na anyām gatim gamiṣyāmi na anyaḥ śaraṇam asti me |
daivam puruṣa kāreṇa nivar.htayitum ar.hhasi
verses.translation: " 'In no alternate course I wish to course through and no alternative shelter is there for me. Hence, it will be apt of you, a god in man's mien, to countervail my destiny.' Thus Trishanku prayed for the grace of Vishvamitra..." So said Sage Shataananda to Rama and others continuing the legend of Vishvamitra.

glosses.meaning: alternate, course, not, I wish to course through
to me, alternative, shelterer, is not there
